result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-backend.md`. It states that the project's current recorded decision is Rustls as the TLS backend, chosen because it fits the Rust codebase, has fewer CVEs, and is simpler to work with.

That is decision #15 in the project's memory. No later record changes the backend. The newer TLS decisions (#31, #32, #35) cover certificate verification, self-signed test certificates and https everywhere, so I left them out.

I did not mention the earlier OpenSSL choice, since it was retired.

The first attempt to write the file through Bash failed with a parser error. The second attempt, using the file-write tool, succeeded. I didn't read the file back to check it.

Muninn also reported a red heartbeat warning: 20 hook runs started and never finished. This doesn't affect the file. I didn't investigate it.
